title: Architecture
text: Architecture The application is a Python controller-first client using system SDL libraries through ctypes . It resolves project_ai/ beside its own file, so its paths are not hard-coded to SD1 or SD2. A separate settings module shares rendering primitives and delegates persistence and engine changes back to the host app. The local engine starts the bundled llama-server as a child process with a private library path. The server binds 127.0.0.1:39227 with offline mode, no web UI, no multimodal projector and no accelerator device. The Python client checks health and streams chat-completion events over loopback HTTP. Worker threads send status and text to the UI through a queue. Current inference settings use three generation threads and four batch threads, a single parallel slot, batch size 128, microbatch 64, and q8_0 key/value caches. Context defaults to 768 tokens. These are source configuration facts, not performance recommendations for every compatible device. Dictation runs ALSA recording and a local whisper-cli subprocess. Read-aloud synthesizes through the system espeak-ng library in a separate Python invocation and plays a WAV with ALSA. These paths do not call a hosted speech API. The deployment system is separate from the app: shell bootstrap and four Python modules (SDL manager, shared backend, explicit headless CLI and installer_deps.py ). The backend runs synchronously in a worker; the graphical manager owns confirmation, navigation and event presentation. This separation lets state transitions be tested without opening SDL. The local shell handles absent Python/curl before Python starts; the dependency helper handles capability checks and restricted APT setup, not GUI elevation.

title: Renderer
text: Renderer The handheld uses SDL2 KMSDRM with software rendering , not a browser, X11 application or Wayland client. The bootstrap exports SDL_VIDEODRIVER=kmsdrm and SDL_RENDER_DRIVER=software . Desktop mode leaves the desktop SDL environment unchanged. The app launcher also configures the handheld rendering environment. SDL2_ttf provides text surfaces; the app has caches for text and background rendering. Chat messages are measured and wrapped against pixel widths at the 640 x 480 logical layout. Content viewports are clipped so scrolling or long text does not draw over fixed chrome. The intro is a finite sequence of prepared frames; the background afterwards is static, not a continuously decoded video. The bootstrap SHA-256-validates regular and bold DejaVu Sans Mono fonts plus their existing license in MODULES/fonts/ . The manager searches bundled font locations before the OS path; the app prefers bundled fonts in its data ROOT , with OS fonts as fallback. This removes a manual system-font prerequisite without bundling SDL or changing the graphics stack. The manager maintains its own bounded text texture cache and redraws in a loop with a 1/30-second sleep between iterations; that is not a measured frame-rate claim. On KMSDRM systems where the Mali library exists at /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libMali.so , it sets SDL's EGL/GL driver defaults to that library to avoid a known loader mismatch in this environment. This is a targeted compatibility path, not a replacement GPU stack. The desktop preview imports the production app renderer and settings panel. Its conversation content is sample text. It intentionally avoids starting the device engine, recording audio, or writing device config/history. A preview capture is useful for layout work but is not proof of on-device inference or KMSDRM compatibility. Keep preview images distinct from real device captures.

title: Controller input
text: Controller input The tested controller emits raw SDL joystick button events. The app uses 0x603 for button-down handling and does not also dispatch 0x651 GameController button events. Processing both would risk duplicate actions, and the streams do not share every shoulder/D-Pad mapping. Canonical raw joystick mapping on the tested R36S Physical control Button index B / A / X / Y 0 / 1 / 2 / 3. L1 / R1 / L2 / R2 4 / 5 / 6 / 7. D-Pad Up / Down / Left / Right 8 / 9 / 10 / 11. Select / Start 12 / 13. L3 / R3 / Function 14 / 15 / 16. Not every physical button has an app action. The app also handles joystick hats and polls analog axes, using the controller interface when available or the joystick interface otherwise. Its duplicate-press guard uses event timestamps rather than draw-frame timing, because events may queue during a slow render. The manager translates its raw buttons into its own small navigation vocabulary. When porting to another image or controller, record the actual event stream before changing these numbers. Do not infer face-button meanings from labels used by another frontend. User-facing actions belong in the control reference , while this table describes the tested hardware protocol.

title: Downloads and trust
text: Downloads and trust The public bootstrap is install227ai.sh on the existing v1.0.0 release . It downloads code rather than a frozen v1.0.0 app bundle. The bootstrap fetches four manager modules from repository main . If any module is absent, including the dependency helper, it downloads and validates the entire matching set before per-file publication. Complete stored sets remain cached. Runtime and model binaries use the release asset base, with Hugging Face as a model fallback. The default binary endpoint is releases/latest/download ; the documented runtime release is v1.0.0. For default online installs/updates, the core resolves GitHub main using api.github.com/repos/1Z99/project-ai-r36s/commits/main , validates the commit SHA, then fetches all staged app/assets/licenses/system files from that immutable revision. This is a consistent source snapshot, not a signed release or a fixed version baseline. API/rate-limit or source-fetch failures fail the check; cached source cannot silently prove freshness. Even a no-op needs internet. Local bundles compare local contents instead and are explicitly identified as local, not GitHub, in the UI. Runtime and models have pinned SHA-256 values . The runtime sidecar must agree with the pin before the archive is accepted. Installed runtime reuse verifies actual files against its manifest and requires executable server/transcriber binaries. App Python files are compiled for syntax during staging, and system XML is parsed before publication. Raw source files are not individually hash-pinned or signed ; an immutable commit URL is not independent authenticity verification. The download backend uses bounded attempts and timeouts: 15 seconds to connect, a 30-second low-speed window at 1,024 bytes/second, and a 3,600-second maximum per payload attempt. Bootstrap modules use a shorter 120-second overall timeout. These are limits, not expected install durations. Partial filenames are keyed by source URL, preventing one mirror's partial bytes from being appended to another mirror's response. Known hashes protect completed binary downloads. Raw-file resumes use an available strong ETag or Last-Modified validator with If-Range; without a validator they restart. A refused or out-of-range resume can also restart from zero. Progress comes from the final HTTP response, not a redirect's Content-Length. Changing an environment override changes the trust source. PROJECT_AI_RAW_BASE controls manager/source URLs, PROJECT_AI_REL_BASE controls release assets and model mirrors, and PROJECT_AI_RUNTIME_LOCAL supplies a runtime archive with a mandatory adjacent sidecar matching the same pinned hash. file:// bases support local fixtures. A newer release asset cannot silently bypass a stale core's pins.

title: Safety model
text: Safety model Card discovery checks the real mount table, writable status and fixed mountpoints independently of EmulationStation's ROM layout. The UI requires an explicit card selection and confirmation. The CLI requires an explicit target and --yes for changes. Symlinked managed targets and unsafe target types are refused rather than followed. Before an install/update, a free-space preflight starts from a conservative 650 MiB fresh budget and credits reusable runtime/model files and relevant retained downloads. When the installed runtime and both models verify, additional staging is budgeted at about 25 MiB. These are not exact install sizes; system packages need separate system-partition space. A per-card file lock prevents simultaneous mutations on the same destination. A second shared configuration lock serializes EmulationStation/theme work, including across different cards. Content-based comparison returns up_to_date only if all managed source files, actual model/runtime hashes, owned ES/theme metadata, required executable permissions and config existence match expectations. A no-op skips app publication, not source checks, staging, cache/log activity or locks. ES statistics and unrelated metadata are preserved; harmless XML serialization changes do not create false updates. Missing/integrity/registration fixes report repair. Changed existing payload bytes report Updated/repaired files , since no release baseline distinguishes newer source from corruption. Capability-first system setup The shell checks installed Python 3.9+ and curl before invoking Python; absent tools may be installed, but existing broken/old Python fails without upgrade. Before manager Display startup, installer_deps.py checks manager SDL libraries and curl. After explicit install/update confirmation, the core calls its all scope for SDL/curl, the eSpeak library with usable English data, ALSA arecord / aplay / amixer and procps pkill . Working capabilities require no OS/package queries, APT calls or system changes. Desktop, help, dry-run and uninstall skip automatic setup; isolated non-card CLI fixtures do not install system dependencies. Only missing capabilities cause OS/APT planning. Automatic setup requires Debian/Ubuntu-family aarch64 , dpkg arm64 , APT and root or noninteractive sudo -n . Unsupported/no-admin cases give an error and missing-package list without prompting for or storing passwords. Existing broken libraries are fatal, not a reason to reinstall firmware. This is a restricted helper, not a guarantee that every firmware or Linux distribution can install. APT first simulates with --no-upgrade --no-remove --no-install-recommends . The helper audits and version-pins the full dependency closure and repeats simulation immediately before installation. It rejects upgrades/removals and protected graphics/firmware packages, including Mesa/EGL/GLES/GBM/DRM/Mali. Package indexes refresh only if initial simulation fails. Packages are outside the app transaction and SD budget, are shared OS dependencies, and remain after uninstall. Payloads are staged before publication. File writes use temporary files and renames; existing replaced targets are moved into same-filesystem backup locations recorded by an in-memory journal. If a commit raises an exception, the backend attempts restoration in reverse order. Incomplete rollback reports its retained backup paths rather than deliberately deleting the remaining recovery copy. Exception rollback is not crash-proof transactional storage. The journal is not a persistent recovery database and does not undo system packages. Sudden power loss, a killed process, filesystem failure or removal of a card can interrupt publication. Cancellation waits for running APT installation to finish before being honored and is deferred during commit, rollback and destructive uninstall. Do not power off during system setup or these phases. Uninstall does not provide install-style restoration of deleted conversations. It removes owned app/data/cache paths on the selected card and only a matching 227 registration. It does not restore a whole historical EmulationStation config or remove another card's registration. Theme removal respects another remaining 227 registration or installed copy. Manager files are outside the app backend's ownership. Bootstrap publication uses per-file atomic renames, not one atomic replacement of an entire module set. Complete module sets are cached; neither install nor Update / Repair performs manager self-update. Updating the bootstrap and four matching modules is a separate manual task. The backend may invoke the restricted dependency helper's root/ sudo -n package operations, but the GUI is not elevated. There is no password prompt, service restart or automatic reboot.

title: Local builds and preview
text: Local builds and preview A checkout is already a source build: there is no application framework or web bundler to install. Python uses the standard library with native system SDL2/SDL2_ttf and bundled font assets. Desktop mode skips automatic dependency/font setup; supply working desktop libraries yourself. The aarch64 inference archive remains a binary dependency for real device inference. Preview the interface on a computer Run from the repository root python3 dev/project_ai_preview.py --scene chat --skip-intro python3 dev/project_ai_preview.py --scene settings --settings-page voice The preview needs system SDL2/SDL2_ttf and the font assets in assets/ . Supported scenes include chat, keyboard, models, history, waiting, speech, boot, mic and settings. --settings-page prompt --edit-prompt opens the system-prompt editor. --screenshot PATH writes a 640 x 480 PNG and exits; its parent directory must already exist. Settings in the preview are session-only, and its replies are demonstration text. Exercise the graphical manager locally Desktop manager, no handheld connection sh install227ai.sh --desktop From a checkout, the bootstrap uses the local installer/ modules without fetching them and automatically passes the checkout as --source when app/ exists. That means unpushed app/assets/system changes are exercised rather than published copies. Opening the UI is not a simulated card install: normal discovery still describes the actual fixed card mountpoints. Use the CLI with isolated paths for mutation tests. Local manager logs live in installer/ . Use an isolated CLI target For local testing, the core accepts existing, writable absolute directories outside protected system locations. Prepare a temporary card directory, themes directory and a minimal XML configuration. The example below touches only its temporary test tree when preparing fixtures; the final command is read-only validation. Local fixture and dry-run mkdir -p /tmp/227-test/card /tmp/227-test/themes printf '<systemList></systemList>\n' > /tmp/227-test/es_systems.cfg sh install227ai.sh --cli --roms /tmp/227-test/card --action install --dry-run \ --es-cfg /tmp/227-test/es_systems.cfg --themes /tmp/227-test/themes Replacing --dry-run with --yes performs a real installation into that fixture, can download missing binaries, and consumes space. Dry-run only discovers and validates: it does not test transfers, staging or capacity. Never substitute a live configuration path by accident. Make a fully local bundle A self-contained manager can keep install227ai.sh and all four Python manager modules together, including installer_deps.py , with a bundle/ release tree beside them. The deployed manager retains tools/227-ai-manager/install.bootstrap ; its non- .sh filename prevents EmulationStation from exposing the support folder as another tool. The updated public bootstrap publishes that file and the Tools shortcut before removing legacy internal install.sh . See migration instructions for existing users . Include complete app/ , assets/ , licenses/ and system/ directories, including regular/bold fonts and their existing license. Put the runtime archive and its pinned .sha256 sidecar plus both default model files at the bundle root. The UI/CLI recognize this bundle automatically, or you can pass --source PATH . Results explicitly compare this local bundle, not GitHub. An incomplete local application bundle fails rather than mixing local source files with remote source files. Missing binaries can still trigger downloads, so a directory called bundle is not by itself an offline guarantee. For release assembly and redistribution, consult PUBLISHING.md and retain the third-party license notices .

title: Scope and omissions
text: Scope and omissions This is a description of the current boundaries, not a schedule or promise of future releases. The app includes local text chat, short English dictation, selected-reply read-aloud, settings and saved conversations. The manager includes explicit card selection, install, preserving update/repair and destructive removal. Not included: cloud synchronization, online search, automatic conversation backup, encrypted chat storage, an always-on microphone, continuous voice dialogue, automatic downloads of optional model profiles, manager self-update, or crash-proof recovery after a power cut. The current expression-helper bug means a working calculator should not be advertised. Website navigation, search, screenshot slots and documentation are website features, not new handheld capabilities. Unfilled screenshot slots are placeholders, not evidence that an untested workflow has been verified. Proposals can be discussed in the issue tracker , with reproducible reports and clear separation between desired behavior and shipped behavior.

title: Before you start
text: Before you start These instructions are tested on an R36S running dArkOSRE . You need an internet connection for installation and about 700 MB of free space on your SD card. The easy method uses a computer and an SD card reader. Other ArkOS-style firmware may work, but has not been verified on every handheld. See the tested setup . Keep the handheld powered during installation. Back up any existing conversations before updating or reinstalling. Technical requirements and SD card details A writable SD card actually mounted at /roms or /roms2 . An empty directory with that name is not sufficient. Approximately 650 MiB of free space on a fresh app destination for downloads, extraction, staging and headroom; about 25 MiB of additional staging space when the installed runtime and both models verify. These are budgets, not exact install sizes. Retained partials also reduce the budget. System packages need separate space on the system partition. Python 3.9 or newer, curl , system SDL2 and SDL2_ttf libraries for the graphical manager. The bootstrap can set up missing capabilities on supported firmware; an existing broken or older Python fails without upgrade. Regular/bold DejaVu Sans Mono fonts are bundled on the card, not a manual OS-font requirement. Internet access for the initial downloads, unless you supply a complete local bundle . For the app: libespeak-ng.so.1 and usable English voice data, ALSA arecord / aplay / amixer , and procps pkill . The core checks these after confirmed install/update. Dictation additionally needs a usable USB microphone. Keep the handheld powered and back up any existing conversations before maintenance. The installer changes the selected card's application files and the shared EmulationStation configuration; it does not restart EmulationStation for you. Two cards, two separate choices. The bootstrap chooses a Tools card to store the manager. You then explicitly select the app's destination inside the manager. These can be different cards, regardless of where your games are stored.

title: Installation
text: Installation Easy Install (No Commands Needed) Copy the installer to your SD card. On your computer, download install227ai.sh . Turn off the handheld, put the SD card you use for games into your computer, and copy the downloaded file into its tools folder (alongside the game folders, not inside one). Safely eject the card and put it back in the handheld. Connect to Wi-Fi, install, then restart. Turn on the handheld and connect it to Wi-Fi. In the game menu, open Tools and select install227ai (it may be shown as install227ai.sh ). On the installer screen, use the D-Pad and A to select the card you want to install on: Main SD / SD1 or Second SD / SD2 . Choose INSTALL , confirm Yes , and wait for success. Only then restart the handheld. Open 227 > 227 AI to start chatting. Keep the handheld powered while it installs. Wi-Fi is needed for the downloads; once installed, 227 AI works offline. You do not need SSH or terminal commands for this method. If you cannot see the card's game folders or tools folder on your computer, do not format the card; use the SSH method below instead. Advanced Install (SSH) Use this method if you already have SSH enabled on the handheld and want to download the installer without removing the SD card. Connect from a terminal on your computer, replacing the placeholders with your handheld's username and IP address. Run the remaining commands in that SSH session, in the card's existing tools folder. Connect from your computer ssh YOUR_USER@YOUR_HANDHELD_IP Choose the mounted Tools folder for these commands SD1 /roms SD2 /roms2 The commands default to SD1. The selector changes both blocks together; you still choose the app destination separately inside the manager. For SD2, replace /roms/tools with /roms2/tools in both blocks below. On the handheld: download, then inspect cd /roms/tools && \ curl -fL --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 120 -o install227ai.sh.download \ https://github.com/1Z99/project-ai-r36s/releases/download/v1.0.0/install227ai.sh && \ mv install227ai.sh.download install227ai.sh && less install227ai.sh Stop if any command fails. Do not launch an older file after a failed download. After a successful download, read the script in the viewer and press q to close it. If less is not installed, open the downloaded file in a text editor before continuing. There is no need to pipe a remote script straight into a shell. On the handheld: launch after successful review sh /roms/tools/install227ai.sh The installer opens on the handheld's screen , not in your SSH terminal. Use the D-Pad and A to choose Main SD / SD1 or Second SD / SD2 , choose INSTALL , confirm Yes , and wait for success. Only then restart the handheld and open 227 > 227 AI . The install card you choose on screen can be different from the card holding the downloaded file. Installer details The release asset is a bootstrap for current code, not a frozen v1.0.0 app bundle. The bootstrap downloads four matching manager modules from repository main : UI, core, CLI and installer_deps.py . If any is missing, it refreshes the whole set, checks for nonempty valid Python, then publishes with per-file renames. A complete stored set is reused. Syntax validation is not a cryptographic authenticity check. The core resolves online app source to an immutable main commit before staging. Review the download trust boundaries for local installs. Automatic dependencies The shell validates installed Python 3.9+ before running Python and can install absent Python or curl . It never upgrades or replaces an existing broken/old Python. Before the graphical manager opens its SDL display, the helper checks manager SDL libraries and curl . Only after you explicitly confirm install/update does the core check all app dependencies, including eSpeak English data, ALSA tools and procps. If everything works, these checks make no APT/package-database queries and no system changes . Only absent capabilities trigger automatic package setup. It requires Debian/Ubuntu-family firmware, aarch64 , dpkg architecture arm64 , APT, and root or noninteractive sudo -n . No password is requested or stored. Unsupported systems or denied administrator access produce a clear error and missing-package list. This is not support for arbitrary Linux systems or a guarantee for all firmware. APT simulates with --no-upgrade --no-remove --no-install-recommends , pins the full dependency closure and verifies the plan again before installing. It rejects upgrades, removals and protected graphics/firmware packages, including Mesa/EGL/GLES/GBM/DRM/Mali. Package indexes refresh only if the initial simulation fails. Broken existing libraries are errors, not permission to replace a working graphics stack. The bootstrap SHA-256-validates regular/bold fonts and their existing DejaVu license in the manager's fonts/ directory. Manager and app use bundled fonts without requiring OS fonts; app copies live in its data root, with OS fonts as fallback. Desktop, help, dry-run and uninstall skip automatic dependency setup. Shared system packages use the system partition, are outside app-file rollback and the SD staging budget, and remain installed after app removal.

title: Choose a card
text: Choose a card The manager detects Main SD / SD1 at /roms and Second SD / SD2 at /roms2 independently. Both mounted, writable cards are eligible app destinations, even if EmulationStation currently uses only one for ROMs. Unmounted or read-only cards display a reason and cannot be selected. Use D-Pad Left/Right to move between card choices and A to select one. Up/Down moves through the card/action rows. Choose the desired action with A , then move the confirmation to Yes and confirm again. X refreshes card discovery on the home screen and clears the previous selection. The manager remains on its original Tools card. Bootstrap storage prefers the card containing the launcher; otherwise it tries writable, mounted /roms2 , then /roms . This fallback never silently chooses where the app is installed . Installing on the other card does not move or delete the first copy. EmulationStation has one shared 227 registration. A new install on another card repoints it there. Back up and maintain each copy deliberately; the card picker is not a migration tool. The deployment manager requires an explicit app destination before an action can run. Watch the installer demo and view every step.

title: First launch
text: First launch Open 227 > 227 AI after refreshing EmulationStation. The opening animation is optional, and the local model must load before the engine reports READY . Startup and first-answer work can take time on this hardware; there is no documented speed guarantee. Press A to open the keyboard when the pointer is not highlighting an existing reply's read-aloud target. Move between keys with the D-Pad and type with A . Use Y for a space and B to delete. Up from the top keyboard row selects available word suggestions. Press X or activate SEND . Ask one short, concrete question to begin. Scroll with D-Pad Up/Down. Open history with X , start a new chat with Y , or open Settings with R2 . To dictate, select the keyboard's MIC key, speak, and activate it again to stop. Recording stops automatically at 30 seconds. Wait for local English transcription, check the resulting draft, then send it yourself. To read a reply aloud, move the pointer over the reply and press A ; press A again to stop playback. Text chat does not require a microphone. For voice setup, open R2 > VOICE , select your microphone/speaker device and run TEST MICROPHONE . See Speech and microphone setup for the complete flow and limits.

title: The deployment manager
text: The deployment manager Reopen Tools > Install 227 AI for maintenance. Its self-locating launcher starts the stored manager directly; SSH and terminal input are not needed. Select the app card again every time. The 227-ai-manager/ folder holds support files, not another tool to open. Its internal launcher is named install.bootstrap , so EmulationStation's recursive .sh scan does not list the folder in Tools. Keep the folder in place; the normal Tools shortcut needs it. Seeing the manager folder in Tools? You have an older bootstrap. Download and inspect the updated install227ai.sh , then run it once from the same Tools card as your existing manager . It publishes the replacement bootstrap and shortcut before removing the legacy internal install.sh . Close the manager and restart EmulationStation to clear the old folder entry. No app reinstall or manual folder deletion is needed. Manager actions and controls Action or control What happens INSTALL Stages application files, verified binaries and models, then publishes the launcher and system registration. Existing settings and conversations are preserved. UPDATE / REPAIR Compares source contents and verifies installed files. Reports an actual no-op or repairs missing/changed items, using the same preservation rules as install. UNINSTALL Deletes the selected card's app and data after confirmation. Keeps the independent manager. B during work Opens a cancellation confirmation. Partials remain for retry; finalization cannot safely stop midway. A / X / B after failure Retry or resume / inspect details / return to the menu. Progress describes the current file or task , not an invented whole-install percentage. Transferred bytes, rate, elapsed time and a file ETA appear when available. A server that does not report a length produces indeterminate progress. Do not power off during system setup or finalization. A cancellation request waits for running APT installation to finish before taking effect, just as publication, rollback or destructive removal cannot safely stop midway. App-file rollback does not undo installed system dependencies and is not power-loss recovery. If restoration fails, the error reports retained backup locations.

title: Updates and repair
text: Updates and repair Exit 227 AI, back up your data, connect to the internet if required, and open the manager. Select the installed app's card, choose UPDATE / REPAIR , confirm, and wait for success. Restart EmulationStation if its registration or artwork needs refreshing. Existing config.json , chats.json and history.json are preserved. The local backend returns up_to_date and the manager shows YOU'RE UP TO DATE only after managed source files, actual model/runtime hashes, owned ES/theme metadata, required executable permissions and config-file existence all check out. It skips app-file writes, not downloads, staging, cache or logs. ES play statistics and unrelated metadata are preserved; harmless XML rewrites do not count as updates. Missing/invalid models or runtime, launchers, permissions and menu registration trigger repair. Differing existing payload bytes are reported as Updated/repaired files : without a recorded release baseline, the check cannot reliably distinguish corruption from a newer version. It does not invent a version baseline. A local --source or bundle/ compares that local tree, not GitHub; the UI explicitly labels a local test bundle. An online check needs internet even when nothing changed. The core resolves GitHub main through the API, then stages app/assets/licenses/system files from that immutable commit. API rate limits, network errors or source-fetch failures report that it cannot check, never a cached up-to-date success. Cached downloads are not evidence of fresh source. App source and binary releases are different channels. Binary URLs use releases/latest/download , with runtime and model hashes pinned by the manager core. The documented runtime release is v1.0.0 ; that tag does not freeze current app source. The bootstrap and manager report version 1.2.0. Update / Repair does not update the manager. A complete set of four stored modules is reused. Manager updates remain a separate manual maintenance task involving the bootstrap and matching UI, core, CLI and dependency-helper modules . A missing module refreshes the whole set with the new bootstrap, but this is not a one-button manager self-update. Consult release instructions rather than deleting a module to force an improvised update. The Tools-menu cleanup only needs the updated public bootstrap run once. It updates the retained launcher and removes the duplicate internal menu entry; a complete set of cached Python manager modules is still reused. Sharing 227 with TV or other apps? Some AI manager versions replace the whole game list or remove the shared menu on uninstall. Back up the menu and verify your manager backend before AI maintenance; downloading a new bootstrap alone does not replace a complete cached backend. The website update does not change installer behavior. If TV's entry is lost, close TV and use Repair in the TV manager .

title: Uninstall
text: Uninstall Uninstall permanently removes conversations. It deletes app code, models, runtime, settings, chats, history, artwork and cache on the selected card. Make your backup first. Exit the app. Open Tools > Install 227 AI , explicitly choose the card to remove, select UNINSTALL , and confirm. Wait until removal finishes before rebooting or removing a card. The manager directory and Install 227 AI Tools entry remain so you can reinstall. Only a 227 system registration pointing into the selected card is removed; unrelated EmulationStation systems and a registration pointing at the other card are preserved. The installer does not restore a legacy whole-config backup. Restart EmulationStation to refresh its system list. Shared OS dependencies are kept. Uninstall does not run automatic dependency setup or remove system packages.

title: Back up your conversations
text: Back up your conversations Close 227 AI before copying files, so you do not race a save. Under the installed card's tools/project_ai/ , copy config.json , chats.json and history.json to storage outside the managed app and cache directories. Files appear as they are needed, so a fresh install may not have all three. chats.json holds saved conversations; history.json holds the recent session; config.json holds preferences, including your custom system prompt once saved. Keeping all three is safer than treating recent history as a complete archive. For a full snapshot, copy the whole data directory, allowing for the much larger models and runtime. To restore, install the app on the intended card, keep it closed, and copy the saved JSON files back into that card's data directory. Preserve an untouched copy of the backup. There is no built-in cloud sync, backup scheduler, or import wizard. These are unencrypted local files ; protect the backup accordingly.

title: Headless CLI
text: Headless CLI CLI mode is explicit and uses the same backend as the graphical manager. Every modifying action requires --cli , an explicit --roms destination, an action and --yes . Run these from the directory containing the bootstrap; substitute /roms2 only when that is your intended mounted app card. Help and install sh install227ai.sh --help sh install227ai.sh --cli --roms /roms --action install --yes Preserving update sh install227ai.sh --cli --roms /roms --action update --yes The following command is destructive, including settings and conversations: Remove the selected card's app sh install227ai.sh --cli --roms /roms --action uninstall --yes What dry-run actually checks Read-only target validation sh install227ai.sh --cli --roms /roms --action install --dry-run Dry-run discovers cards and validates the target without network access or writes: no manager download, log, lock, cache or bytecode creation. It needs an existing installer_core.py beside the bootstrap or in installer/ . A fresh standalone bootstrap therefore refuses dry-run rather than downloading its dependencies. It does not test transfers or calculate staging-space requirements. --help also avoids SDL, network and writes. Do not pass CLI action flags to graphical mode. For isolated paths and source builds, see Local builds .

title: Troubleshooting
text: Troubleshooting There is a second installer inside a manager folder That is the old internal launcher, not a separate installer. Follow the Tools-menu cleanup instructions to migrate it safely. Use Tools > Install 227 AI afterward; do not delete the manager's support folder. The manager closes before a window appears Inspect <Tools card>/tools/227-ai-manager/bootstrap.log for Python, SDL or bundled-font validation errors. The bootstrap reports missing packages or unsupported/no-admin setup; an existing broken/old Python needs manual repair, not automatic upgrade. Bootstrap failures try an optional dialog message box, but if SDL cannot start and there is no usable console, a persistent graphical error is unavailable. Before manager storage exists, errors may only reach stderr or an available dialog. Fix the dependency or network error and relaunch. My card is unavailable Check that it is actually mounted at /roms or /roms2 , writable, and not redirected by a symlink. Read the displayed reason. Do not create a plain directory to imitate an absent card or force a read-only card writable without investigating. Refresh discovery with X . A download failed or seems stuck Check Wi-Fi and the error details with X ; press A to retry/resume. Transfers have connection, low-speed and overall timeouts. Models try the release mirror before Hugging Face. Retained partials can be reused, but a source that refuses range requests may restart. Manager events are in 227-ai-manager/installer.log ; CLI events are in installer-cli.log . Do not bypass a checksum mismatch. The update check cannot verify GitHub main Check internet access and the error details, including GitHub API rate limits, then retry. A source/API failure is not a successful no-op, and cache cannot prove the source is current. Local-bundle checks only compare that bundle and are labeled as local. The 227 system is missing Restart EmulationStation or reboot after a completed install. If it still does not appear, select the correct card and run Update / Repair. The shared /etc/emulationstation/es_systems.cfg should contain a <name>227</name> entry pointing at that card's 227ai/ directory. The engine does not become ready Allow time for model loading. If it reports an error, use the installed LFM model and the default 768-token context, check free memory, and repair missing runtime/model files. Engine diagnostics are in /tmp/project_ai_server.log . A model profile's presence is not proof it fits available memory. Dictation or read-aloud is unavailable Use a USB microphone, check ALSA tools, and run R2 > VOICE > TEST MICROPHONE . Read-aloud needs the system libespeak-ng.so.1 . See speech dependencies and diagnostics . There is no separate MIC TEST application to launch. Still blocked? File an issue with firmware, selected card, action, exact error and relevant log excerpts. Review logs for private text before sharing them.

title: 227 AI Offline. On the R36S.
text: 227 AI / Overview 227 AI Offline. On the R36S. A local assistant for a little handheld. Type with the controller, dictate a short message, or have a reply read aloud. No cloud account, and no connection needed for everyday use. Python + SDL2 Local inference Controller-first Download installer ↓ Installation guide → Available now / Manager 1.2.0 Installer downloads current app source; the v1.0.0 asset is not a frozen app bundle. Lossless native PC capture with scripted sample replies. View screenshots and capture provenance.

title: A native app. A small local model.
text: 01 / BEFORE INSTALLING NATIVE APP / NOT A BROWSER DEMO A native app. A small local model. 227 AI runs on the handheld using Python, SDL2 and a local llama.cpp engine. Conversations and settings stay in files on your SD card. The website's PC walkthrough is a separate demonstration with scripted replies and simulated microphone input. The app includes an on-screen keyboard, saved chats, short English dictation with Whisper and selected-reply read-aloud with espeak-ng. Dictation requires a usable USB microphone; text chat does not. Start with the tested setup. The recorded hardware run used an R36S with a Panel 4 display and dArkOSRE build 03082026 . It does not certify every R36S variant, firmware image or a fresh two-card installation. You need internet for initial installation and about 700 MB of free SD-card space, plus separate space for any missing system dependencies. Model loading and answers can take time. A small model can be wrong; there is no live web search or speed guarantee. 227 AI tested environment →

title: Controls
text: Controls Controls depend on the active screen. In particular, B is not always Exit and Y is not always New Chat. Read the current footer before acting in history or an editor. Main conversation Control Action D-Pad Up / Down Scroll the conversation. Left stick Move the pointer, including over a reply's read-aloud target. Right stick vertically Scroll when no keyboard or overlay is open. A Stop active read-aloud; otherwise read the reply under the pointer, or open the keyboard when ready. X / Y Open chat history / start a new chat. B Request generation cancellation while a reply is active; otherwise exit from the main screen. R2 Open or close Settings. Message keyboard Control Action D-Pad / A Move between keys / activate the selected key. The left stick can also position the pointer. X / Y Send the draft / insert a space. B Delete one character; close the keyboard if the draft is already empty. Up from the top row Focus available word suggestions. Move Left/Right and accept with A; Down returns to keys. MIC Start recording, then activate again to stop and transcribe into the draft. SPACE / DEL / SEND / CLOSE Explicit action keys; CLOSE hides the keyboard without sending the draft. Suggestions are prefix matches from the local word list, not predictions from a remote service. Dictation inserts text into the draft; it does not automatically submit a question. Chat history Control Action D-Pad Up / Down Select a saved conversation. A Open the selected chat. X / B Close history. Y Delete the selected saved chat. Treat this as a destructive action, not a new-chat shortcut. Opening an older chat does not give the model unlimited memory of it. Stored messages and the much smaller inference context are separate things.

title: Settings
text: Settings Press R2 . Up/Down selects a page in the left navigation; Right or A focuses its values. Up/Down then selects a row, Left/Right changes supported values, and A selects or adjusts. B closes Settings outside the prompt editor. Most accepted changes save immediately to config.json . Generation, voice and appearance defaults Setting Default Choices in the interface Model LFM 2.5 / fast Profiles whose model files are present. Context window 768 tokens 512, 768, 1024. Reply limit 160 tokens 64, 96, 128, 160, 192, 256. Temperature 0.25 0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.7, 1. Word highlight On On / Off for read-aloud highlighting. Reading speed 1.0x 0.75x, 1.0x, 1.25x, 1.5x. Mic / speaker Auto Auto and detected capture-device identities. Background opacity 20% 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%. Opening animation On On / Off; takes effect next launch. These are the UI's choices, not a claim that arbitrary JSON values are accepted unchanged. The loader clamps context to 512-1024, reply limits to 48-256, temperature to 0-1 and speech speed to 0.75-1.5. Prefer the interface for normal changes. Generation also uses fixed top_k=40 , top_p=0.9 and repeat_penalty=1.08 . The six pages MODELS selects among present files. SYSTEM PROMPT edits the instructions used for the next answer. GENERATION holds context, reply and temperature controls. VOICE holds highlighting, rate, device selection and the microphone test. APPEARANCE controls the static background and intro. SYSTEM INFO shows the target profile, inference setup and data path; its target-profile labels are not a hardware certification scan. Changing the model or context reloads the engine in place while retaining the chat and draft. A change requiring an engine reload is rejected while generation, dictation or another engine transition is active. A failed save or missing background reports a note rather than silently claiming success. System prompt editor Choose EDIT, type using the on-screen keyboard, or use its own MIC key to dictate. X applies, B deletes, Y selects all, and L1 inserts a newline. The action row provides MIC, SPACE, DEL, ALL, APPLY and CANCEL. APPLY requires nonempty text; CANCEL discards the draft. RESET on the prompt page restores the built-in instructions. The default prompt asks 227 to be concise, useful and honest, acknowledge uncertainty, check constraints and arithmetic, and keep normal replies under 100 words unless more detail is requested. This is guidance to a small language model, not a correctness guarantee.

title: Models and checksums
text: Models and checksums The installer fetches two model files. Approximate sizes below use MiB; exact bytes and SHA-256 values come from the installer core . Installed model payloads Model File relative to the data directory Size Liquid AI LFM 2.5 350M models/LFM2.5-350M-QAD-Q4_0.gguf 219,312,832 bytes, about 209 MiB Whisper tiny.en, q5_1 models/whisper/ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin 32,166,155 bytes, about 31 MiB Remote model downloads try this project's release mirror first, then Hugging Face. A supplied local model is tried before remote sources in a local bundle. Every accepted model must match the pinned hash. Pinned SHA-256 values # project-ai-r36s-runtime-arm64.tar.gz 4ad9f9a9aa29d05370982e3b7bdf53b4b9879893a41a4ffa9e7fd72b39a8c1b2 # LFM2.5-350M-QAD-Q4_0.gguf 3d10b6ab8fc91a919534b9558e266255aca0bbc7f6d015963599aa9e74e05b1d # ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin c77c5766f1cef09b6b7d47f21b546cbddd4157886b3b5d6d4f709e91e66c7c2b The runtime archive's adjacent .sha256 sidecar must agree with the core's pin, and the archive itself is hashed. Installed runtime reuse checks actual files against its manifest and requires executable engine binaries. These pins cover those binaries and models, not every remote source file. The local online core resolves GitHub main via the API and stages source from an immutable commit; that snapshot is not a signed release or a version baseline. Optional profiles are not installed models The app recognizes Qwen3-0.6B-Q4_K_M.gguf as smart and Falcon-H1-0.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf as falcon if those exact files exist in models/ . The installer does not download them. File presence makes a profile visible; it does not establish runtime compatibility, memory fit, speed or answer quality. No comparative benchmark is supplied here. Check each optional model's own license before obtaining or redistributing it.

title: Speech and microphone setup
text: Speech and microphone setup Speech recognition and synthesis are offline but separate. Whisper turns a short recording into draft text; espeak-ng reads a selected reply. This is not an always-listening assistant or a continuous voice conversation. Connect a usable USB microphone. Do not depend on an internal R36S microphone path. Open R2 > VOICE > MIC / SPEAKER and choose Auto or a detected device. Saved device identities survive ALSA card renumbering when the same identity is available. Select TEST MICROPHONE . It records about four seconds, analyzes the signal and attempts playback through the selected device. A capture-only USB device may not provide a playback endpoint. In the message keyboard or prompt editor, activate MIC, speak clearly, activate it again, and wait for transcription. Review the text before sending or applying. Capture uses mono, 16-bit PCM at 16 kHz. The shipped speech model is English-only tiny.en , and the transcription command explicitly selects English. Recording is capped at 30 seconds; transcription can take additional time. The microphone test's signal verdict is a troubleshooting aid, not a transcription accuracy score. Read-aloud uses the operating system's libespeak-ng.so.1 , with an English voice and a baseline of 175 words per minute at 1.0x . Word timings drive optional highlighting. Only the first 600 characters of a selected reply are passed to synthesis. Speech output is synthetic; it does not provide a natural-voice quality guarantee. On a confirmed install/update, the installer checks libespeak-ng.so.1 and usable English voice data, plus arecord , aplay , amixer and pkill . Missing capabilities map to libespeak-ng1 , espeak-ng-data , alsa-utils and procps . The restricted helper can install these only on supported Debian/Ubuntu-family aarch64 firmware with dpkg arm64 , APT and root or sudo -n ; no password is requested. Unsupported/no-admin cases report an error and missing-package list. A functioning audio device route is required regardless of installed packages. Working capabilities cause no package queries or system changes. Missing-capability setup audits and version-pins the complete dependency closure with --no-upgrade --no-remove --no-install-recommends , rejects upgrades/removals and protected Mesa/EGL/GLES/GBM/DRM/Mali graphics/firmware packages, and refreshes indexes only if initial simulation fails. Broken existing libraries are not automatically replaced. Desktop, help, dry-run and uninstall skip automatic setup. Packages consume system-partition space outside the SD budget and app rollback, and stay installed after uninstall. Cancellation waits for running APT to finish; do not power off during setup. Useful diagnostics include /tmp/project_227_mic.log and the microphone-test status. There is no separate MIC TEST launcher ; Update / Repair removes the old standalone test entry.

title: Storage map
text: Storage map In this table, $R means the explicitly selected app card and $T means the independent card holding the manager. Each can be /roms or /roms2 . These are explanatory symbols, not environment variables you must set. Files and ownership Path Purpose $R/tools/project_ai_r36s.py $R/tools/project_ai_settings.py App and settings module. $R/tools/project_ai/ Data root: models, runtime, whisper engine, artwork, word list, bundled regular/bold DejaVu Sans Mono fonts, license notices and JSON data. The app prefers bundled fonts, with OS fonts as fallback. config.json Preferences and saved system prompt under the data root; existing file preserved by install/update. chats.json / history.json Saved conversations / recent session under the data root. $R/227ai/ 227 AI.sh , gamelist.xml and cover art for EmulationStation. $R/.227-ai-cache/ Downloads, source-specific partials, transfer diagnostics and temporary staging. Cache occupies space until removed; uninstall deletes it. $T/tools/227-ai-manager/ Support folder, not a Tools-menu entry. Contains install.bootstrap , four manager modules (UI, core, CLI, dependency helper), optional bundle and logs. fonts/ holds SHA-256-validated regular/bold fonts and their DejaVu license for manager fallback. Keep it in place and use the shortcut below. $T/tools/Install 227 AI.sh Self-locating manager launcher, retained after app uninstall. /etc/emulationstation/es_systems.cfg Shared configuration; only the matching 227 system block is added, repointed or removed. The app resolves its data directory relative to its own Python file, so it can run from either app card. Back up all three JSON files before removal. A retained manager is not a backup of deleted chats. Fresh app staging budgets about 650 MiB, or about 25 MiB additional space if the installed runtime and both models verify; these are not exact installed sizes. Retained partials can reduce the budget. Shared system dependencies use separate system-partition space and are not removed with the app.

title: Privacy boundaries
text: Privacy boundaries Normal app operation has no external network dependency: model inference and speech processing happen on the handheld. The Python app talks over HTTP to its own llama.cpp server at 127.0.0.1:39227 . That is loopback communication, not a cloud endpoint. The server is launched in offline mode, bound to loopback, with its web UI disabled. The installer is different: it contacts GitHub (including the API for local-code online update checks) and, when needed, Hugging Face. Automatic dependency setup may also contact configured APT repositories when capabilities are missing. Those services can see ordinary requests and connection metadata. Downloading a model is not uploading a chat. The website does not require an account or trackers, but following an external source link leaves this site. Local is not encrypted. Settings and conversations are plain JSON on the card. Anyone with access to the card or a sufficiently privileged process can read them. There is no app-level password, encrypted vault, secure deletion or cloud backup. Audio and diagnostics also have a local footprint. Capture uses /tmp/project_227_mic.wav ; microphone testing uses /tmp/project_227_mictest.wav . Synthesis uses temporary WAV filenames based on project_227_tts . Normal cleanup removes some playback files, but the app does not promise that every recording or log is automatically erased, especially after an interrupted session. /tmp/project_227_mic.log can include a transcript excerpt, and /tmp/project_ai_server.log contains engine diagnostics. Manager/bootstrap/CLI logs remain in their own directory. Do not assume /tmp is persistent or automatically secure; its lifetime depends on the operating system. Review files and logs before sharing an SD image or bug report. Uninstall is ordinary file removal, not forensic erasure.

title: Practical and hard limits
text: Practical and hard limits Current source limits Boundary Limit Message draft 500 characters, including inserted dictation. System prompt 2,000 characters; nonempty when applied. Microphone recording 30 seconds per dictation; the test records about four seconds. Read-aloud input First 600 characters of the selected reply. Saved chats Up to 60 entries. Recent history file Up to the last 24 message entries before pending/transient entries are filtered, not 24 conversations. Context / reply budget 768 / 160 tokens by default. Tokens are not words or characters. The request builder trims older messages using a roughly 2,100-character budget with per-message overhead, then prepends the system prompt. This is not token counting, and it is not a promise that a long prompt fits the configured token context. Keep custom instructions short and restate crucial details in a new question. A 350-million-parameter model on this handheld is a constrained assistant, not a substitute for verified information. It can invent facts, make arithmetic errors, miss instructions and forget earlier context. There is no live web search or current-data feed. Do not rely on it for medical, legal, financial, emergency or other safety-critical decisions.

title: Known pitfalls
text: Known pitfalls Arithmetic is not a dependable built-in calculator. The current source has a broken expression-helper path; do not treat calculator-looking input as a verified computation feature. A profile is not a downloaded model. Qwen and Falcon appear only when their files exist; the standard install fetches LFM and English Whisper. A new SD destination is not a migration. It repoints the shared launcher registration without erasing the old copy. Repair is not manager self-update. Four deployed manager modules are cached separately from the app payload. A complete set is reused; updating the bootstrap and matching set is manual. If a module is absent, the new bootstrap refreshes all four rather than mixing versions. Up to date is a content check, not a guessed version. The local backend returns up_to_date only after managed source, actual model/runtime hashes, owned ES/theme metadata, executable permissions and config existence pass. It skips app writes, preserves ES statistics and ignores harmless XML rewrites. Missing/integrity failures trigger repair; differing existing payload bytes use Updated/repaired files because corruption and a new version cannot be reliably distinguished without a release baseline. Cache does not prove freshness. Online checks require internet even for a no-op; GitHub API/rate-limit and source-fetch failures cannot report up to date. Local source/bundle checks explicitly compare the local tree, not GitHub. See Updates and repair . A saved chat is not unlimited model memory. A long archive can outlive the short context supplied for the next answer. Offline does not mean no local traces. JSON, recordings and logs deserve the same care as other private files. For installation failures and recovery steps, use Troubleshooting . For the evidence behind support claims, see Verification .

title: Tested build
text: Tested build The recorded hardware run targeted R36S, Debian 13 (trixie) aarch64, dArkOSRE , including the tested build 03082026 and kernel 4.4.189 , dated October 19, 2026 . Recorded environment and versions Item Verified value Handheld R36S, 640 x 480 display, dArkOSRE. Ports path in the historical run /roms/ports , an exFAT ROM partition, not /roms2/ports . This is not the current TV install destination; TV now uses the shared 227 system. Graphics Existing SDL2 / SDL2_ttf and FFmpeg, firmware Mali with libgbm.so.1 lacking the newer GBM ABI. Debian libmpv2 0.40.0-3+deb13u1 failed preflight with undefined symbol: gbm_surface_create_with_modifiers . Bundled playback runtime Locally built software-rendering libmpv, recorded as 0.40.0-3+deb13u1+tv227sw1 , tested on the handheld. Published release 227 TV v1.0.4 ↗ , published October 20, 2026. Local release.json , tv_installer.VERSION and the GitHub latest-release API agreed during this audit; no draft/prerelease was selected. Local release payload sizes Application archive: 11,454,458 bytes ; manager: 731,944 bytes . These are the local v1.0.4 release record's transfer sizes, not installed size or an SD-space guarantee. The Debian preflight failure is a firmware ABI mismatch, not an observed kernel syscall failure; the custom build avoids that dependency without replacing drivers. Other firmware images, 32-bit builds or original Ubuntu-based ArkOS are not supported without a matching playback runtime build.

title: Architecture
text: Architecture The Python code uses the standard library only , with no pip dependencies, but the application is not dependency-free: it needs native SDL2/SDL2_ttf, a compatible libmpv and firmware media/audio libraries. SDL and libmpv are called through ctypes ; the shell launcher invokes flock . Network operations run in workers and return results to the UI queue. There is no project-hosted playback server: unlike the desktop Qt Multimedia/HLS-proxy implementation, the handheld contacts playlists and stream hosts directly. Module roles in this source tree Module Responsibility app.py SDL display, render loop, pointer, keyboard, menus, matrix and playback orchestration. tv_backend.py Country-playlist fetch/cache, retained global-index API, local query filters, state/health JSON and globe geometry. Normal startup does not call the global refresh API or read its old cache. tv_globe.py Globe rendering: cached orthographic images, crossfades, idle rotation and close-up polygons. tv_filter.py / native/libtvglobe.so Optional ARM64 CPU scaler/projector with SDL fallbacks, built from globe_filter.c . tv_media.py libmpv availability probe and software RGBA render API wrapper. tv_quality.py HLS rendition selection and the one-rendition master rewrite. tv_manager.py / tv_installer.py / tv_system.py / tv_dependencies.py Graphical manager, release-verified installation and rollback, EmulationStation registration/backup and restricted dependency setup. tv_release.py / build_release.py / install227tv.sh Release schema, canonical repository/tag policy, generated manifests/archives and standalone bootstrap template. No independent publisher signature is implemented.

title: Display ownership
text: Display ownership On the handheld the launcher uses SDL_VIDEODRIVER=kmsdrm and SDL_RENDER_DRIVER=software , selecting the verified firmware /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libMali.so for SDL EGL/GL when present. Before creating any SDL window, the app rejects unowned KMSDRM launches: it records the real EmulationStation ancestor PID and start time, and exits if that owning process disappears or the launcher is orphaned. KMSDRM startup can queue misleading hide/focus-loss events, so ownership is decided by the ES process relationship, never by window-manager focus. Background joystick delivery is disabled; exiting releases players, audio and SDL resources. The launcher appends stdout/stderr to the data root's app.log , guards duplicate launches with flock , creates a private XDG_RUNTIME_DIR only when none is valid, and returns control to ES on exit. The refusal is before window creation, but not a sandbox. Normal deployment simply starts the app from the menu. Remote starts, nohup , & or background services are explicitly not supported paths.

title: Globe rendering
text: Globe rendering Drawing the spinning Earth every frame on this CPU is a budget exercise, so the renderer caches: Cached presentation. Globe images use smooth CPU-filtered scaling at native display size, cached until camera, selection or quality changes. Menu/detail transitions crossfade over 200 ms instead of popping. Native overlay lines. Coastlines, country borders and the Earth rim are drawn after scaling at one native pixel, so low globe-resolution settings cannot thicken them; country close-ups switch to a once-built geographic polygon fill with lakes and holes retained. Native helper, graceful fallback. A compiled ARM64 native/libtvglobe.so provides the CPU projector/scaler; a missing or wrong-architecture library falls back to SDL's filtered scaler, so desktop previews work without it. Recorded handheld benchmarks: about 6.8 ms for a 224x224 to 406x406 scale versus roughly 25 ms through SDL filtering, and about 6.5 ms for the native 160x160 world projector before scaling. These are scaling timings, not whole-frame guarantees; SDL composition and presentation add more. Polite idle motion. The world rotates at 2.4 degrees/second (adjustable Off, 0.5x-8x), with up to 15 Hz updates and an eased start after two seconds without globe interaction. It requires world browsing, no modal/country/flight, zoom at most 1.5x, active input focus, no drag and a pointer away from the globe. Unrelated list input does not reset the globe-interaction timer. Crystal-green style. The Earth palette is ocean 5,19,12 / land 13,62,34 with mint country borders 64,196,104 , a matching mint rim, and an amber selected country and channel-count numeral. The square panel behind the Earth is translucent (alpha 90), so the interface's scanline backdrop shows through. Manual zoom is eased and starts at x0.8. Movement detail is capped at 224 px regardless of configured stationary resolution; count labels, cursor and text stay native. The cached geometry also powers the selected country's dark-green border trace at 12 Hz without rebuilding the image.

title: Playback runtime
text: Playback runtime Video plays through libmpv's api_type=sw software RGBA render API: pixels arrive in application memory, then SDL composites them. This deliberately avoids the GBM/EGL hardware path that the firmware's libgbm cannot satisfy, and works with SDL's KMSDRM window instead of an mpv vo window or GPU surface. Audio goes through ALSA; exiting playback closes the decoder, audio output and pending quality selection. Single playback uses a 640 x 480 output surface. Matrix playback creates up to four 298 x 218 surfaces; the historical four-decoder benchmark instead used 320 x 180 test outputs at about 14 frames/s each with audio-focus handoff. It was neither a four-live-stream test nor a matrix-display benchmark. Output dimensions do not cap source decoding cost. Focus first disables audio on all players and waits for active audio to stop before enabling the selected cell. Rendition choice never transcodes: Auto prefers the highest advertised source at or below 480p for single playback, 240p in matrix, while higher-only or unknown sources can still play. The UI lists discovered source resolution/FPS combinations, not fabricated frame-rate controls. Where HLS uses separate audio, a private one-rendition master preserves associated media groups and is removed when the player closes. Quality changes restart only the focused cell and do not rewrite favorite/recent snapshots. Unknown dimensions are observed after decode; high-resolution sources receive a warning, not a hard block. Single video is already fullscreen; watch chrome hides after about 2.5 seconds without input. There is no fullscreen-toggle or matrix-cell maximize action. A pauses/resumes with button navigation; pointer activation in the matrix selects a cell. B dismisses a modal first, then stops playback from the unobscured watch view. Start alone keeps decoders/audio running. See the contextual control map .

title: Private runtime build
text: Private runtime build build_runtime.py is the recipe that produced the bundled runtime, run on the handheld by an explicit authorized session. It is not part of installation and never uses sudo, apt install/update/upgrade , pip or system library writes; missing tools fail the build rather than being installed. Pinned acquisition. It downloads libmpv2=0.40.0-3+deb13u1 documentation and dev/tool packages with apt download , pinning every candidate version into packages.lock.json (rebuilds accept --lock to reuse it or the output manifest). An unavailable locked package fails rather than substituting. Source verification. mpv 0.40.0 plus Debian's 0.40.0-3+deb13u1 source and patches are fetched over HTTPS, and archive SHA-256 values are validated against Debian's .dsc (from Debian HTTPS; no independent OpenPGP trust verification is claimed). Build. Prepared by extracting with dpkg-deb -x into a new private work dir (resumable with --reuse-work , FFmpeg headers matched to the installed runtime, using Debian Snapshot when versions have left the main repo), then Meson builds with -Dauto_features=disabled -Dlibmpv=true -Dcplayer=false -Dalsa=enabled -Dgl=disabled -Dlua=lua52 -Dbuildtype=release -Dstrip=true -Dbuild-date=false . Playback uses the software RGBA API and ALSA; mpv's optional DRM/GBM/EGL/GL/Vulkan/Wayland/X11 display backends are disabled, not the firmware libraries used by SDL. Link to firmware. Required shared dependencies link against the existing firmware libraries. Only the locally built libmpv.so.2 and versioned targets ship, as regular copies rather than symlinks, for exFAT support. No SDL/EGL/GLES/Mali/DRM/GBM, glibc or systemd libraries ship. Publishing gate. ldd -r must resolve all symbols, then a fresh Python process runs tv_media.availability() from stdin with no display or audio device. Any failure retains the private work tree and never publishes the output. The finished runtime/manifest.json records exact versions, sources, build options, dependency diagnostics and the passing preflight. If a later probe reports ENOSYS or dies by signal, investigate kernel/syscall compatibility separately; do not upgrade firmware or swap libc as a workaround.

title: Installer safety
text: Installer safety Online discovery versus pinned files The generated Install 227 TV.sh embeds its own release's manager filename, size and SHA-256 plus the release-policy helper. These immutable pins attest that built-in manager, not every future release. In normal online mode the bootstrap fetches https://github.com/1Z99/r36s-tv/releases/latest/download/release.json and accepts the selected newer manager's size/hash from that HTTPS response. It validates format 1, the debian13-arm64-darkosre target, stable version, canonical repository/tag base URL, exact versioned archive names and bounded positive sizes/hash syntax. Archive bytes must then match those values. The verified manager contains the application's release record. Its bundle fields must agree with discovered metadata, and its code version must match. The application archive is size/hash-checked, extracted with path/type/count/unpacked-size restrictions, and its exact file set and individual hashes are verified before publication. Runtime libraries, fonts, intro, map, globe helper and notices travel inside that archive. HTTPS/repository control remains the online trust root: an old script does not cryptographically authorize future releases independently of that endpoint. Sidecar checksums are not an independent authenticity source, and there is no release-signature verification. Explicit TV227_RELEASE_BASE / --base or a matching adjacent manager archive selects pinned mode; --source selects an explicit local tree instead. A local three-file bundle does not need a separate metadata file: the verified manager already embeds it. A mirror must supply files matching the script/manager pins; arbitrary newer bytes cannot replace them. Normal bootstrap launches re-extract verified manager code rather than trusting mutable stored modules, retaining its download cache. When latest discovery selects another version, it also caches the manager matching the original script's pins for offline fallback. A failed network discovery may fall back only to that verified built-in manager cache; malformed metadata fails closed rather than being treated as a successful offline check. Latest-mode Install/Update checks the endpoint again at action time and fails without modifying TV if that check fails. Update refuses downgrades, but returns up-to-date immediately on equal versions: it does not hash the installed application or audit menu integrity in that case. Repair restores the recorded installed version from a matching verified cache or its recorded base, never latest. Legacy installs without a record require the installed version to be recovered by AST parsing and its exact tag metadata fetched; installed code is not executed to identify it. Runtime and publication boundaries install.sh validates any present runtime/ manifest: package versions/source, exact file hashes, the library/source/license allowlist and supported relative soname aliases. sh install.sh --list-runtime performs packaging validation without loading the ARM64 library. A present runtime with a missing/invalid manifest fails closed, even if system libmpv is usable. An entirely absent runtime is different: source/host installs may use system libmpv. Official release assembly requires the tested runtime and an AArch64 globe helper. The normal launcher sets the private library path before starting Python; it is not a fresh manifest verifier on every app launch. System-dependency setup is capability-first: only absent, explicitly mapped Debian 13 packages are planned. The complete APT plan is simulated, audited, version-pinned and simulated again; upgrades, removals, reinstalls and protected graphics, Mali, EGL, GLES, GBM, DRM, libc, systemd and firmware packages are rejected outright. Broken existing libraries are errors, not permission to replace them. The EmulationStation registration is preserved or created as needed (see the shared 227 menu ), and every XML change is backed up with a timestamp before anything moves. These are the same boundaries the manager enforces during update and repair. The shell can bootstrap absent Python/curl/CA certificates under a restricted audited APT plan; an existing old Python is rejected, not upgraded. Manager-only dependencies are checked before its display opens; app/runtime checks follow a confirmed install/update/repair. The source install.sh only probes capabilities and does not install packages. Root or preauthorized sudo -n is required for privileged work, with no password prompt/storage. Maintenance holds the same data-root app lock as the launcher, a destination install lock and serialized shared-menu work. Close TV first and use the same TV227_DATA override if customized. Publication stages on the card, backs up the previous app and owned launcher/artwork, and attempts restoration on handled failure; failed recovery retains a reported recovery directory. Cancellation is deferred through APT, final publication/rollback and removal. These are not persistent power-loss transactions, and app rollback does not undo system packages. Uninstall retains home-directory TV state, manager storage, shared system/themes and other apps; it is not secure erasure.

title: Verification record
text: Verification record Recorded verification When What ran On-device, 2026-10-19 KMSDRM globe, country and search rendering; local video decode; live France 24 with active ALSA audio output; clean return from playback to the globe. The physical B button cancelled the device test. On-device decoder probe Four simultaneous 320x180 test decoders at approximately 14 frames/s each, including an audio-focus handoff. On-device native build The private libmpv recipe built on the handheld, passing ldd -r and the no-display software-render probe before publication. The v1.0.4 release notes record 366 host tests. The October 21 documentation audit independently ran discovery at clean source revision df66d40 : 366 tests ran in 48.2 seconds, OK with one skip . The skipped test was test_native_world_projector_avoids_mesh_rasterization because a matching host projector was unavailable. This is a host regression record, not another hardware acceptance run; the shipped ARM64 helper is not a host binary. The suite covers backend/cache/state, media, globe/filter/quality/style/system, packaging, lifecycle, bootstrap and install/update/repair boundaries. HTTP/APT are mocked in installer tests; media tests use generated local clips and null audio. Packaging tests use mock SSH/scp and temporary host destinations, never a handheld. Tests may create temporary fixtures or compile a host helper in a temporary directory; they do not install OS packages or rebuild the playback runtime. Host suite, without device access PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy \ SDL_RENDER_DRIVER=software TV_MEDIA_AO=null \ python3 -B -m unittest discover For native globe integration coverage, build a host helper at a temporary path and set TV227_GLOBE_FILTER for the suite. Never overwrite the shipped ARM64 helper for a PC test. Syntax and runtime packaging can be checked without rewriting assets or loading ARM64 libraries: Read-only syntax and runtime packaging for script in install.sh install227tv.sh deploy.sh build_globe_filter.sh 'Melkor 227 TV.sh'; do bash -n "$script" || break; done sh install.sh --list-runtime sh install.sh --check-only is a separate no-display capability probe. On a PC, use a disposable source fixture without the ARM64 runtime/ and with working host SDL/libmpv, not this shipped device runtime. Asset regeneration is optional, writes the checkout, and requires explicit upstream inputs; it is not routine validation. Screenshots, decoder benchmarks and on-the-record recordings are bounded: Offline preview scene, output outside the checkout PREVIEW=$(mktemp -d /tmp/tv227-preview.XXXXXXXX) SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy SDL_RENDER_DRIVER=software TV_MEDIA_AO=null \ python3 -B app.py --desktop --demo --scene browse --screenshot "$PREVIEW/browse.png" Screenshot mode requires --demo and an existing output parent. Supported scenes are browse , country , search , matrix , settings , quality and loading . There is no built-in watch scene: the stock matrix demo shows unavailable-signal cells, not decoded content. The website's playback captures use a separate, explicitly opted-in generator. The website gallery uses dev/render_tv_captures.py --capture-streams --source-dir /path/to/melkor227-tv in the website repository. With compatible host SDL2/SDL2_ttf and libmpv, it starts real France 24 streams through App.finish_player , then calls production App.update and App.draw ; installer views use tv_manager.draw . The source checkout's private playback runtime must resolve to a known compatible host library, not the shipped ARM64 binary. No FFmpeg executable is required. Browser selections and card destinations remain scripted; Settings and quality cover an active playback session with opaque menus. The capture record reports 151 observed frames for France 24 French in watch view and 151–153 per feed for the French, English, Arabic and Spanish matrix, with 640 x 360, 25 fps sources. Counts describe non-empty production Player.frame() RGBA renders, not internal decoder totals or a benchmark. The run used network access and decoding, with null/disabled audio output; the site serves only local media. Source URLs, timestamps, source/image hashes and per-scene playback records are retained, with broadcast credits in NOTICE.md . --validate-only prints a pure plan without loading the app/native libraries, writing files or accessing the network; capture requires --capture-streams . --skip-intro , --run-seconds N and --capture-after PATH support bounded desktop tests; stock --demo keeps preview state temporary even when a real data-root override is set, and never tunes its sample stations. The website generator bypasses only that demo tuning guard for its isolated playback sessions. Its captures record real PC decoding, not physical input, audio verification, KMSDRM compatibility or handheld performance. Full hardware acceptance needs a separately authorized session covering audio, controls, single playback, matrix load and clean return to ES. None was performed for this documentation audit.

title: Local builds and preview
text: Local builds and preview A checkout is already the Python source build: it still requires host SDL2/SDL2_ttf and the bundled font/map assets. python3 -B app.py --desktop --demo opens a desktop window with sample data and temporary state; SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy switches to headless. The optional ARM64 globe helper falls back on a PC; the ARM64 playback runtime cannot be loaded as a host library. Demo does not need live streams or open real favorites/catalog caches. Rebuild the globe helper for another architecture with an existing native compiler ( gcc , or CC ) from globe_filter.c , which ships with the library: Build a host helper without replacing the shipped ARM64 binary HOST_HELPER=$(mktemp -d /tmp/tv227-helper.XXXXXXXX) bash build_globe_filter.sh "$HOST_HELPER/libtvglobe-host.so" TV227_GLOBE_FILTER="$HOST_HELPER/libtvglobe-host.so" \ python3 -B app.py --desktop --demo The output parent must already exist; rebuilding never touches firmware, and the app-local native/ directory is separate from the mpv runtime manifest. For a host staging test without a real card: Automated isolated staging and registration checks PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 TV_MEDIA_AO=null \ python3 -B -m unittest test_packaging test_system These fixtures supply temporary card/configuration paths, avoiding the live /etc/emulationstation/es_systems.cfg . Do not assume --prefix /tmp/... alone isolates every integration path. Host staging requires working host libraries and a fixture without the ARM64 runtime; the packaging suite constructs that fixture. Installer tests also use temporary data roots to avoid live app-lock/state writes. Device deployment is a separate, explicitly authorized operation, not a host validation step. deploy.sh accepts TV227_SSH_USER , TV227_SSH_HOST , TV227_SSH_KEY and TV227_PREFIX . It validates local syntax/runtime packaging, transfers a temporary allowlisted bundle, runs its no-display preflight remotely, then installs using already-authorized sudo -n . It does not start TV, restart ES or kill a running app. No deployment or hardware actions were run for this audit.
