title: Scope and omissions
text: Scope and omissions Shipped: the atlas, country-only loading, favorites/recent snapshots, local search filters, manual HTTP health rechecks, fullscreen single video, experimental matrix playback with focused audio and rendition preferences, CRT overlay, world-spin settings, shared 227 registration and release-verified maintenance. Not shipped or promised: worldwide search/preloading, universal firmware compatibility, transcoding, a hard SD-only decoder limit, matrix maximize, station uptime/speed guarantees, signed release authentication, power-loss-safe rollback or automatic playback after install. Same-version Update is not an integrity audit; use Repair. The desktop plugin keeps its own life: Omarchy hides the HLS proxy, QtMultimedia embedded playback, and the looping health scanner behind desktop windows. When those parts change upstream, the handheld port considers them separate projects, not silently shared behavior.

title: Before you start
text: Before you start This release targets an R36S, aarch64, running dArkOSRE based on Debian 13 (trixie) , including the tested build 03082026 and kernel 4.4.189 . Original Ubuntu-based ArkOS, AmberELEC, 32-bit images and arbitrary clones are not supported by the shipped binaries. The manager checks the platform before downloading/installing the application; the smaller manager may already have downloaded by then. The normal one-file install needs internet. Live television and new country lists also need a connection; Wi-Fi adapter support comes from your firmware, not TV. Keep the handheld powered during installation and leave at least 200 MiB free on the destination card as a practical starting budget for downloads, unpacking and rollback, not an exact installed size. Missing system packages need separate space on the system partition. Technical requirements Python 3.10 or newer, plus the firmware's SDL2 and SDL2_ttf libraries. Working SDL KMSDRM and Mali drivers on the handheld for display. Root or existing noninteractive sudo -n authorization for installation; no password is requested or stored. A writable SD card actually mounted at /roms or /roms2 . Wi-Fi for live streams and for downloading any missing Debian 13 packages.

title: Installation
text: Installation One-file installer (online, recommended) Download Install.227.TV.sh ↗ from GitHub Releases. With the handheld powered off, copy it to the games card's existing tools folder alongside the game folders. You can rename it Install 227 TV.sh for a tidy menu. Safely eject the card, put it back, and boot the handheld. Use the release installer, not a source-code ZIP, the source install227tv.sh template or install.sh . If your computer cannot see the games partition, do not format the card; use a reader/OS that can access it. Enable Wi-Fi. Open Tools > Install 227 TV . Choose the destination card: use Left/Right on the destination row to select SD1 ( /roms ) or SD2 ( /roms2 ). An unmounted or unwritable card is unavailable. If 227 AI already has a 227 menu, choose that card. Select Install , confirm Yes , and wait for completion. Reload or restart EmulationStation's menu yourself when ready. Open 227 > 227 TV . TV does not install into Ports. The installer downloads a controller-driven manager, then the complete app, artwork, fonts and matching playback engine. Downloads are checked before use. Obtain the script from the project's trusted release page: checksums detect mismatched files, but there is no independent publisher signature. See the build notes for the online and offline trust chains. Offline Application Bundle For a card without network access, download three matching files from the same release page and put them together in the card's tools directory: Install 227 TV.sh melkor227-tv-manager-1.0.4.tar.gz melkor227-tv-1.0.4-darkosre-arm64.tar.gz The two archives make application installation offline; they do not contain a replacement operating system or every Debian package. Missing compatible system packages still come from the Debian repositories, and existing working firmware dependencies are reused. Keep matching files together. A matching manager archive beside the script automatically selects the local, pinned release rather than latest-release discovery. The script verifies that manager; its embedded release record verifies the application. No separate release.json download is needed for this three-file method. To return to normal online updates later, move the two copied archives out of the installer's folder and reopen the script with Wi-Fi. The manager requires an explicit destination before any action runs. Update, Repair and Uninstall TV complete the four actions. Advanced mirror override Advanced users can set an explicit HTTPS mirror or file:// release directory. This pins Install/Update to that release rather than discovering latest: Point the bootstrap at a hosted or local release TV227_RELEASE_BASE="https://github.com/1Z99/r36s-tv/releases/download/v1.0.4/" \ sh 'Install 227 TV.sh' --cli --roms /roms --action install --yes Use a matching script and both archives. An override does not disable size/hash checks and is not a way to make an old script accept arbitrary new files. Repair still targets the installed version.

title: Choose a card
text: Choose a card The manager treats SD1 ( /roms ) and SD2 ( /roms2 ) as independent destinations; unmounted or read-only cards cannot be selected. Installing on the other card does not move or delete an earlier copy. The card picker is not a migration tool. Back up and maintain each copy deliberately, and choose the card you intend to update. The bootstrap stores its manager on the card containing the script when eligible, otherwise a writable mounted SD2, then SD1. The app destination is a separate explicit choice. Keep the tools/227-tv-manager/ support folder and Install 227 TV shortcut for maintenance. Both app copies use the same default home-directory TV state, not separate per-card favorites.

title: The shared 227 menu
text: The shared 227 menu If an EmulationStation system <name>227</name> already exists, its directory, command, extensions, theme and unrelated metadata are preserved. For example, it can point to /roms/227ai/ , alongside 227 AI.sh . TV adds only its own launcher, artwork and gamelist entry, preserving 227 AI statistics and other projects . You do not need an existing 227 system or 227 AI. If the system is absent, TV creates it automatically using <card>/227ai/ . Reloading EmulationStation only makes that new menu visible; you do not create it yourself. If 227 is registered on another card, the installer refuses to silently retarget it: choose that card instead. The existing registration must use a direct child of the selected card for the relative launcher. Only TV's own historical Ports entry is migrated, and only when its launcher is identified as TV's file. Unrelated Ports games are never removed, and a Tools fallback remains. Changed EmulationStation XML receives timestamped backups beside the original files. Some 227 AI manager versions can remove other shared entries. Do not assume a newly downloaded AI bootstrap updates a complete cached manager backend. Back up the shared menu before AI maintenance, and verify that manager's preservation behavior separately. If TV's menu entry is lost, close TV and run Repair in the TV manager. TV does not modify AI's manager, models or chats.

title: First launch
text: First launch Open 227 > 227 TV after refreshing the menu. The short 19-frame intro plays on each normal launch; A , B or Start skips it. An empty World list saying Choose a country is normal: startup does not download the world's channels. Press Start , choose Browse countries , move Up/Down and confirm a country with A . This is the easiest first selection; you can explore the globe with the left-stick pointer later. Wait for its channel list. Use Up/Down to select a station and A to watch. Left/Right pages the list. Try another station if the broadcaster is unavailable. Playback already fills the screen. The header, footer and pointer hide after about 2.5 seconds without input. A pauses/resumes; L2 / R2 lowers/raises volume. Press B to stop playback and return to browsing. With no menu open, Y saves/removes the selected station as a favorite; L1 / R1 switches World, Favorites and Recent. To leave TV, use Start > Exit TV , select Exit to EmulationStation and confirm with A . B first clears country/search filters when browsing, then opens the exit prompt from the unfiltered world. Fullscreen watch controls during real France 24 French playback. PC capture, not handheld evidence. Press X to search the channels already loaded for that country , not a worldwide service or a country finder. Search can also filter saved Favorites/Recent. The keyboard opens before loading, but cannot find unseen channels. See the search reference . If playback is slow, try Start > Resolution / frame rate and a lower advertised format, or keep Auto / up to 480p . Some broadcasters offer only HD; TV warns and continues rather than creating a lower-quality stream. Start with one channel before trying the experimental matrix . Launch handheld TV only through EmulationStation. The app needs exclusive use of the handheld display and controller while the menu waits. Do not start it remotely or in the background beside EmulationStation. Desktop previews are a separate developer mode.

title: Update and remove
text: Update and remove Close TV first; the installer does not kill the app, start TV, restart EmulationStation, reboot, upgrade firmware or alter Wi-Fi configuration. Manager actions Action What happens Install Installs beside 227 AI after verifying the application archive; preserves an existing 227 registration. Update In normal online mode, checks the repository's newest stable release, verifies a newer bundle and refuses downgrades. A same-version result is a version check, not an installed-file integrity audit: use Repair for missing/changed files. An offline latest check fails safely; explicit mirrors/local bundles compare their pinned version instead. Repair Restores exactly the installed release, preferring installed-release.json beside the app. It can use a matching verified application cache offline. Without a record, the version is read from installed code without executing it and its exact tag metadata is fetched, so that recovery needs network access. Repair never guesses "latest". Uninstall TV Removes TV's program and launchers, not 227 AI, the shared 227 registration or themes. Favorites, history, catalog caches and preferences in ~/.local/share/melkor227-tv are deliberately retained. B asks to cancel. Downloads are cancellable; an in-progress APT transaction or final publication is allowed to finish safely before cancellation takes effect. On failure A retries, X shows details and B returns to the menu. Installers from v1.0.0/v1.0.1 remain pinned to their own version: replace that Tools script once with the newest Install 227 TV.sh from the Releases page ↗ . From v1.0.2 onward, future stable releases are available through Update in normal online mode; explicit mirror/local-bundle choices remain pinned. Back up before maintenance. Close TV and copy ~/.local/share/melkor227-tv/state.json to a separate safe location; it holds favorites, the last 50 recent stations and preferences. Copy the entire data directory if you also want country caches and health records. State normally lives in the user's home, not on the games card. To restore, keep TV closed and restore the saved files to the same data root, retaining an untouched backup.

title: Dependencies and safety
text: Dependencies and safety The complete app bundle includes its own matching playback engine. You do not need to install a distribution mpv package or replace graphics drivers. Working firmware dependencies are reused; only missing, approved Debian 13 packages may be added after a simulated, version-pinned safety check. Existing broken libraries or a plan requiring upgrades, removals or protected graphics/base-system changes cause an error. Missing Python, curl or CA certificates can be bootstrapped under the same restricted policy; an existing Python older than 3.10 is not upgraded. System packages remain after TV removal and are outside app-file rollback. Do not power off during package setup or final installation. Rollback after a handled failure is not a guarantee of recovery from power loss. The technical safety model explains the boundaries.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Troubleshooting Tools does not show the installer, or 227 is missing Check that the release script is in the games card's existing tools folder and ends in .sh , then reload the menu. A scraped-games-only filter can hide an unregistered script. After successful installation, reload/restart EmulationStation; if TV is still missing, choose its installed card and run Repair. Existing shared 227 directories are preserved, so the path need not literally be 227ai/ . The installer closes before a window appears Inspect ~/.local/state/melkor227-tv/bootstrap.log (or $XDG_STATE_HOME/melkor227-tv/bootstrap.log when overridden). This records early download, Python, platform and pre-display failures. A text error dialog is only available with a usable terminal and dialog utility. Check network access, supported firmware and existing noninteractive sudo authorization; relaunch after correcting the reported error. My card is unavailable, or 227 is registered on another card The card must actually be mounted at /roms or /roms2 , writable and not redirected by a symlink. Do not create a directory to imitate an absent card or format it to fix this. If 227 already points at the other card, choose that card: TV refuses to silently move the shared menu. Where are the other logs and downloads? The graphical manager log is ~/.local/state/melkor227-tv/installer.log ; the launcher appends to ~/.local/share/melkor227-tv/app.log (under TV227_DATA if overridden). Application archives cache on the selected app card at tools/227-tv-manager/cache ; manager archives cache on the bootstrap's Tools card at tools/.227-tv-downloads . Review logs for private URLs and paths before sharing. The installer says a dependency ABI is incompatible Use matching firmware or rebuild the runtime against the tested recipe. Do not replace Mali/GBM libraries or install foreign distribution packages. A download or latest-release check fails Check Wi-Fi, free card/root-partition space and the exact error. In the manager, X opens failure details and A retries. For offline files, use the matching script and two archives from one release. Never bypass a checksum mismatch. Offline Repair needs its installed-release record and matching cached application archive; the bootstrap also needs a verified cached manager. A first-ever one-file launch cannot work offline without the three-file bundle. World is empty, search finds nothing, or a country looks stale Open Start > Browse countries first, and wait for loading. Search only filters the selected country's loaded channels or saved Favorites/Recent; it does not fetch worldwide results. Clear a search with the keyboard's CLEAR then FIND. Country/query filters also apply to Favorites/Recent; use World / clear filters before switching tabs to see all saved entries. Try Refresh selected country online; a failed fetch can retain an older country cache, and some countries have no playlist. A channel buffers, says SIGNAL UNAVAILABLE, or has no sound Try another channel to distinguish a broadcaster/region problem from a connection problem. Reopen the station after checking Wi-Fi. For slow video, choose a lower advertised quality; Auto cannot manufacture SD from an HD-only broadcast. Press A if paused and raise volume with R2 ; in matrix mode, focus a populated cell to hear it. Recheck station health tests HTTP reachability, not working video or audio. TV closes immediately, or competes with EmulationStation Read app.log for a duplicate launch, missing runtime, invalid JSON or display-ownership error. Launch from 227 > 227 TV or its Tools fallback, never a parallel remote/background process. If a normal menu launch still competes, stop testing and report it rather than disabling the guard; multiple sessions can also cause conflicts. Close TV before Repair. Back up malformed state before attempting recovery; do not delete favorites as a first troubleshooting step. Still blocked? File an issue ↗ with firmware/build, architecture, chosen card, installed version, action, exact error and relevant log excerpts. Say whether an image is an offline preview or a real device capture.

title: Advanced CLI
text: Advanced CLI The bootstrap accepts the same actions over SSH through an explicit headless --cli mode, using the graphical manager's backend without opening its display. Changes require --roms and --yes ; substitute /roms2 only when that is the intended mounted app card. Do not start the graphical manager remotely alongside EmulationStation. Read-only destination and 227 registration validation sh 'Install 227 TV.sh' --cli --roms /roms --action install --dry-run Install from a complete local source tree sh install227tv.sh --source /path/to/melkor227-tv \ --cli --roms /roms --action install --yes Remove TV only; saved TV data and 227 AI are kept sh 'Install 227 TV.sh' --cli --roms /roms --action uninstall --yes This is not a write-free standalone-bootstrap command. Bootstrap startup can log, download and replace verified manager files before the CLI dry-run runs. The manager dry-run itself only validates the card and shared-menu destination: it does not install packages, download the application, change menus or prove sufficient staging space. Missing bootstrap tools are not installed in dry-run mode. --es-cfg PATH and --themes PATH support explicit integration/test destinations; use isolated fixtures rather than a live config for host testing.

title: 227 TV Live TV on a globe.
text: 227 TV / Overview 227 TV Live TV on a globe. Spin the world atlas with the controller, pick a country and watch its live stations. No app account or app backend is required: channel lists need internet access, and playback connects to broadcasters' stream servers. It shares the handheld's 227 menu with 227 AI, but works without it. Python + SDL2 Software libmpv Controller-first Installation guide → Field manual → Latest stable: 227 TV 1.0.4 Download the one-file installer from GitHub Releases ↗ and read the guide . The world atlas on a PC, using four authentic France 24 entries rather than a downloaded world catalog. This browser state is scripted. Screenshots and capture provenance.

title: A native app. A spinning atlas.
text: 01 / HOW IT WORKS NATIVE APP / NOT A BROWSER DEMO A native app. A spinning atlas. 227 TV descends from the Melkor 227 plugin in my Omarchy bar: the desktop station atlas where thousands of live TV stations ride a rotatable globe. This is a controller-first Python/SDL2 source port of that plugin for the R36S, not a bit-for-bit reproduction of its Qt/QML version. The handheld UI renders with SDL software rasterization and libmpv's software RGBA API: no Qt, no external player window and no GPU video surface. Each country's channel list is downloaded only when you open it, with a separate 24-hour cache. Favorites and Recent come from saved snapshots without downloading the world list. Startup loads only the local map and saved preferences. France 24 French playing in the production SDL interface on a PC. Provenance and broadcast credits. Built for the KMS display. The app owns the handheld screen exclusively. It records the EmulationStation ancestor that launched it and refuses background or orphaned KMSDRM launches to avoid competing for rendering and controller input. Launch it from 227 > 227 TV , never with nohup or a background service. The historical hardware verification on 2026-10-19 covered globe and country rendering, search, local video, and live France 24 with active ALSA audio. These PC captures are not new device tests. High-resolution streams can be slow, and availability depends on the broadcaster. Read the recorded verification and its limits. Four distinct France 24 language feeds, decoded together on a PC. Not unrelated stations or a handheld performance benchmark. Provenance and broadcast credits.

title: Controls
text: Controls Read the current footer: buttons change meaning in search, menus and playback. These are user-facing actions on the tested R36S, not a universal controller mapping. Navigation and browsing Control Action Left stick Local AI mouse pointer with matched speed and deadzone; hold A over the globe and drag to rotate it. A Watch the selected station in list focus, choose the country at the crosshair in globe focus, or activate the pointer's target. Hold while moving the pointer over the globe to rotate it; release without dragging to pick a country. D-pad List Up/Down selects a row; Left/Right pages by eight rows. In globe focus it rotates the atlas; A then picks the country at the center. Select Toggle globe / list focus. L1 / R1 Previous / next browsing tab. L2 / R2 Zoom out / in while browsing. X / Y Open search / toggle the selected station's favorite status. These shortcuts are not active during playback. Right stick vertically Scroll the browsing list or a menu opened from browsing. It is not a playback-menu scroll control. Start / FN Open the menu. L3 (left-stick click) Play a random station from the currently filtered browsing list. B When browsing, clear country/search filters first; from an unfiltered World view, open the exit confirmation. In a menu, close it (quality returns to Settings). Fullscreen playback and matrix Control Action A Pause/resume the single player or focused matrix player when using button navigation. With the pointer active in the matrix, A selects the cell under it instead; a click in single-channel video pauses/resumes. D-pad / L1 / R1 In the matrix, move between the four cells / cycle backward or forward. Focus controls which cell is audible, not which stream is fullscreen. Empty cells can also receive focus. L2 / R2 Lower / raise saved app volume by 5, clamped to 0-100. The value applies to all players; only the focused matrix cell is audible. Start Open Settings without stopping playback. Resolution / frame rate affects the focused cell. R3 (right-stick click) Pause/resume the focused player, including when the pointer is active. B With a menu open, dismiss it first. With no menu open, stop all players and return to browsing, closing their decoder/audio output and cancelling pending quality work. Fullscreen is automatic. A station opens at 640 x 480; the watch header, footer and pointer hide after about 2.5 seconds without input. There is no separate fullscreen button or matrix-cell maximize action. Menus alone do not stop playback. Stop playback , B from the watch view, switching playback or exiting TV closes players; stale network results cannot restart a stopped session.

title: The three tabs
text: The three tabs WORLD, FAVORITES and RECENT Tab What it holds WORLD The rotating atlas. Clicking a country starts an eased camera flight along the shortest longitude path, then pulls into close-up and reveals that country's channels with the Local AI Matrix glyph scramble, one row at a time. The selected country renders in amber with its channel-count numeral at the country's centroid. FAVORITES Stations you saved with Y . It opens from saved snapshots without downloading the world index. RECENT Up to 50 stations selected for single-channel playback, newest first, from saved snapshots. An unsuccessful tune can still be recorded; starting matrix slots does not add them here. There are three tabs, no Archive tab. World hides stations marked dead by the health checker; saved snapshots can still appear in Favorites/Recent. These tabs do not require a world-index download, but their streams still need network access. Switching tabs retains the country and search filters . To see saved stations from all countries, use Start > World / clear filters , then switch to Favorites or Recent. Merely switching back to World does not clear a loaded country; the menu action does. The channel panel has eight rows and truncates list names to 15 characters. The globe's numeral counts loaded country entries, not confirmed live stations or necessarily the number remaining after search/health filters. Build a watch matrix Select a station while browsing, then choose Start > Add selected to matrix . Repeat for up to four slots, then choose Watch matrix . Slots are session-only, may contain duplicates, and are separate from favorites. Clear matrix clears the queued slots, not players already running; use Stop playback or B to stop those. Use the D-pad or L1/R1 to move focus, or point at a cell and press A. Only that cell supplies audio; focusing an empty slot is silent. All populated cells keep decoding independently. There is no per-slot remove/replace or maximize command: clear the queue and rebuild it, or stop and select a station normally for fullscreen. Four-view mode is experimental and may be too demanding for a particular stream combination. The focused cell has a bright green border. Four distinct France 24 language feeds play in this PC capture ; it is not a handheld performance test.

title: Search
text: Search Press X for the Local AI bold keyboard with its cached green cursor. A types, B deletes and closes the keyboard when the draft is empty, Y inserts a space, and X applies the search. Explicit FIND and CLOSE keys are available in the action bar. Search is a local filter, not worldwide discovery. It matches all typed words, case-insensitively, against station name, country/code, language and tags in the current country list or saved Favorites/Recent snapshots. Available metadata varies by playlist; a language query cannot match missing language fields. The draft is limited to 80 characters. No search text is sent to a remote search service. Choose countries with Start > Browse countries , not the search keyboard. That picker works before any channels load. With an empty World list, search has nothing to match and does not fetch a catalog. CLEAR only empties the draft; press FIND or X to apply that empty filter. CLOSE discards draft edits. Opening a country resets the query and returns to World; late country responses cannot replace a newer selection. FIND applies the draft; CLOSE leaves the field unchanged. This PC browser fixture searches the loaded France entries.

title: Settings
text: Settings Start opens a full-screen menu; d-pad Up/Down selects rows and Left/Right or A toggles values. The menu stays open while you adjust CRT or globe detail. While watching, Resolution / frame rate is the first row. Menu rows and their options Row Options Resolution / frame rate Available for the focused playing station. Auto prefers the highest advertised rendition at or below 480p for single-channel video, 240p in matrix. It is a preference, not a hard HD block. Other rows list real source formats, not invented FPS controls; no transcoding happens. Selection restarts that cell and is not a saved per-station quality preference. Browse countries Open the world list to frame a country directly. World / clear filters Clear the current country list and filters. Random station Play from the currently filtered rows, preferring stations not in Recent when possible. Does not download a worldwide catalog. Add selected to matrix Pin the selected station into one of the 2x2 matrix's four slots (n/4 shown). Watch matrix / Clear matrix Start the queued slots (requires at least one), replacing existing playback / clear the session's slot queue without stopping current playback. Globe resolution 128, 160, 192, 224, 256, 320, 384, 448 or 512 px internal globe size. The choice persists; movement detail is capped at 224 px, and the default renders 160x160 while moving and 224x224 when stationary. CRT overlay Off / On phosphor overlay (default Off for clean playback). CRT intensity Normal / High effect. CRT animation Off / On drifting refresh band and flicker. Earth rotation speed Off / 0.5x / 1x (default) / 2x / 4x / 8x idle world-spin speed; the choice persists in the preferences file. Recheck station health Check up to 12 loaded country stations, oldest checks first, with up to four HTTP workers. This checks reachability and a nonempty response, not decoding, sound or sustained availability. Dead entries are hidden from World, not deleted from favorites/history. Refresh selected country Re-fetch the current country's playlist. Stop playback / Exit TV Stop audio/video without leaving, or open the full-screen LEAVE 227 TV? prompt (Keep watching / Exit to EmulationStation); your favorites and preferences stay saved. Defaults in state.json are volume 70 , CRT overlay Off, Normal intensity, CRT animation Off, 1x (2.4 deg/s) world spin and 224 px stationary globe resolution. Accepted settings save immediately. Idle spin is limited to world browsing: it pauses for globe hover/manual movement, menus, flights, country/close-up views and inactive desktop focus. List navigation or pointer motion away from the globe does not by itself stop rotation. Auto and broadcaster source formats, with France 24 French playback continuing behind the opaque menu. PC capture; no on-device transcoding.

title: Downloads and caches
text: Downloads and caches Country-only loading. Normal startup reads bundled geography, saved state and health records; it does not load the old global catalog.json or fetch channel/stream/feed indexes. Opening a country uses https://iptv-org.github.io/iptv/countries/<code>.m3u , parsed into countries/<CODE>.json in the data root. A cache younger than 24 hours is reused. After expiry, or on Refresh selected country, TV attempts a new fetch; a failed fetch can fall back to the existing cache regardless of age. A first-time 404 produces an empty country cache. Channel selection checks HLS renditions and listed alternatives in the background, preferring a source within the handheld quality target before decoding. Where needed, a private one-rendition master retains separate audio/subtitle groups and is removed when the player closes. Quality changes affect only the focused cell and never saved favorites/history. Unknown dimensions are checked once decoding begins; HD-only streams can still play with a warning and may be slow. This is source selection, not a guarantee that a source under the target exists. The backend also retains a global-index refresh API using iptv-org channel/stream/feed data, with a master-playlist fallback, but normal country browsing does not call it. The previously recorded 13,498 station/feed entries were a historical global-index observation, not today's shipped channel total. Country playlists change and may have limited metadata, duplicates/alternative sources, dead URLs or regional restrictions. Availability depends on the broadcaster.

title: Storage map
text: Storage map Here $C is the selected app card, $T the bootstrap's Tools card (each /roms or /roms2 ), and $H the launching user's home. They are explanatory symbols, not variables you need to set. The two cards can differ. Files and ownership Path Purpose $C/tools/melkor227-tv/ Managed program modules, assets/ , optional globe helper/source, private runtime/ with manifest/licenses/corresponding sources, and release documentation. installed-release.json records the installed release for Repair. Not the preferences directory, even in a source checkout by default. $H/.local/share/melkor227-tv State root ( TV227_DATA overrides it): catalog cache, favorites, recent history, preferences, app.log and app.lock . The launcher appends to the log and uses flock to reject duplicate launches for that data directory; the installer never copies, replaces or deletes saved state. state.json , health.json , countries/*.json Under the data root: favorites, up to 50 recent station snapshots and preferences / reachability records / parsed per-country caches. Legacy catalog.json can remain but is not loaded at normal startup. Matrix slots and query are not persisted. $C/227ai/Melkor 227 TV.sh Default main launcher; an existing shared 227 registration can use another direct child of the selected card. $C/tools/Melkor 227 TV.sh is the app's Tools fallback. Current artwork is images/melkor227.jpg , the unchanged AI cover JPEG, not the old SVG. $H/.local/state/melkor227-tv/installer.log Graphical installer events. $T/tools/Install 227 TV.sh $T/tools/227-tv-manager/ Maintenance bootstrap and extracted manager support files, distinct from the Tools app launcher. Bootstrap-verified manager archives live in $T/tools/.227-tv-downloads/ ; a local offline application may be copied there too. The selected app card's $C/tools/227-tv-manager/cache/ holds verified application downloads and source-keyed partials. $H/.local/state/melkor227-tv/bootstrap.log Early bootstrap/pre-display errors; XDG_STATE_HOME overrides this bootstrap log's parent. The graphical manager's installer log uses the home path above. EmulationStation XML files The shared 227 system and gamelist entries; every change receives a timestamped backup beside the original file. The default state root is shared by both card installs for the same user. TV227_DATA overrides it; the Python app also accepts --data-dir , but the launcher's lock/log follow TV227_DATA . Prefer that environment override consistently for maintenance and launch, and keep it outside the managed program tree. Close TV before backing up at least state.json , or the whole data root for caches/health. Invalid saved JSON raises an error rather than being silently overwritten with defaults. See Update and remove for retained state.

title: Privacy boundaries
text: Privacy boundaries The app has no account, project-hosted playback proxy or telemetry service. Country-list requests go to iptv-org's GitHub Pages host over HTTPS. Selecting a station can contact broadcaster/CDN alternatives and HLS playlists before a picture appears; decoding then fetches media, and manual health rechecking also makes HTTP requests. Those hosts see your IP address and normal connection metadata. Streams and their redirects may use HTTP as well as HTTPS ; catalog HTTPS does not make every broadcast encrypted or trusted. Installation/update discovery separately contacts GitHub's release endpoint and asset hosts. Missing dependencies may contact configured APT repositories; a runtime rebuild also has its own source/package downloads. Release archive verification does not authenticate a third-party channel or promise its safety or availability. Search is local filtering and sends no query to a search service. Favorites, recent choices and preferences are unencrypted local JSON; they are not uploaded by TV, but can identify what you watched. There is no app-level password, encrypted vault, remote wipe or cloud backup. Anyone with access to the data root or backup can read them. app.log and installer.log can contain stream errors, URLs and system paths. Review them before sharing logs or an SD image. Local is not encrypted.

title: Practical and hard limits
text: Practical and hard limits Current source limits Boundary Limit Watch matrix Up to four independent players in a 2x2 layout, with 298 x 218 render surfaces and one audible focus. Auto prefers up to 240p sources; higher-only sources can still decode. Smaller output surfaces do not remove source decoding cost. Station recheck Batched per menu invocation (12 stations per scan step). Country list Eight visible 42-pixel rows; 15-character list names with full names in playback settings. Quality cap Auto prefers the highest rendition at or below 480 p (240 p in matrix); HD-only sources are not blocked, only warned about. Country cache Parsed JSON per country, 24-hour freshness; older data may be reused after fetch failure. Country downloads are limited to 8 MiB; the old global catalog is not used at startup. Search / history 80-character search draft; up to 50 distinct recent station snapshots, most recent first. Recent records selection, not proof that decoding succeeded. Device test --device-test --run-seconds N is bounded to 0 < N ≤ 60 . Owner-verified decoder numbers exist for one handheld: four simultaneous 320x180 test decoders at about 14 frames/s each, including an audio-focus handoff. That was a decoder probe, not a four-station live-stream or matrix-display benchmark, and it is not a speed promise for any network stream.

title: Known pitfalls
text: Known pitfalls Matrix mode is experimental. Treat four-station watching as a probe, not a settled feature. HD-only streams are slow. The warning-and-continue path is intentional; scaling cannot make every HD source smooth on this hardware. Offline browsing is not offline television. Saved favorites/recent and cached country lists can be viewed offline. New lists and live media need a network; demo scenes never tune their sample stations. Signal unavailable means just that. The catalog indexes stations that may be dark; availability is the broadcaster's, not the app's. Never launch TV in parallel with the menu. KMSDRM is not a desktop compositor; a background nohup launch races EmulationStation for rendering and input. The app refuses unowned launches, but two ES sessions or background processes can still collide. The station list is a snapshot. Country playlists refresh on a 24-hour country cache or manual Refresh; freshly open stations can be missing and dark ones can linger. For install failures use Troubleshooting ; for the evidence behind the hardware claims, see Verification .
